headline: AMD has reportedly raised the price it charges graphics-card makers for GDDR6 memory, a cost that is likely to reach buyers.
score_reason: Curator score kept at 5: a single trade-press report with no confirmation from AMD in the article, but the price effect on graphics-card buyers is direct.
importance_line: Buyers of Radeon graphics cards, especially the current RX 9000 series, could pay more because Wccftech expects the card makers to pass the cost on, but the article carries no confirmation from AMD.
summary: Wccftech reports, citing Board Channels, that AMD told its board partners, the companies that build and sell Radeon graphics cards, that it raised the price of GDDR6 graphics memory from 1 Oct 2026, which Wccftech says leaves them little choice but to pass the cost on to buyers. Wccftech adds that Nvidia has reportedly sent no such notice for its dearer GDDR7 memory and may not raise those prices this year, and that other parts such as circuit boards have also become more expensive.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Wccftech relays Board Channels (and Bench Life for the wider price rises); no confirmation from AMD or Nvidia in the article. The 1 Oct date is the effective date of the hike per the report; the news of it is new today.
